key_insight: A microgram-scale acoustic resonator prepared in non-Gaussian Fock states enables quantum-enhanced, phase-insensitive sensing of weak signals beyond the standard quantum limit.
engineering_relevance: The work points to practical high-frequency quantum sensors for detecting forces, gravity-related signals, and other weak perturbations using massive mechanical systems.
method: Use a transmon qubit to optimally control the resonator into Fock states with up to seven phonons
Let the weak resonant signal interact with the prepared mode and then measure the phonon-number distribution
Train a neural network to estimate signal strength directly from measured responses without an analytical system model
evidence_signal: Bayesian analysis reports a Fisher information five times the vacuum value and a 7.0 dB improvement in signal-amplitude sensitivity, with the machine-learning estimator achieving the same gain and about half the systematic bias.
watch_item: Performance is currently limited by state-preparation infidelities, so real-world deployment will depend on improving control fidelity and robustness.
paper_title: Quantum-enhanced mechanical sensing with machine-learning estimation
